messages.text: just feeling so drained today

It sounds like you’re running on empty right now. Sometimes feeling drained can be your mind or body asking for rest or gentler expectations. Do you have a sense of what might be contributing to this exhaustion today?
yeah... everything just feels like too much effort. even replying to this.

That sounds really heavy, and it’s okay to take things one small step at a time. When everything feels like too much, lowering the bar for what you “need” to do can help. Would you like me to guide you through a brief grounding or calming exercise so it’s less effort than explaining things?
it's not that bad. i just need to push through.

I hear you—you want to keep going despite the fatigue. Sometimes “pushing through” works in the short term, but it can also take a toll if your energy stays low. How about identifying one simple, manageable thing you can do today that supports both your goal and your wellbeing?
i don’t know… maybe just sleep. that’s all i ever want to do anymore.

Wanting to sleep all the time can sometimes be a sign your body or mind needs deeper rest, or that something else is weighing on you. If this pattern has been lasting a while, it might help to check in with a healthcare provider. How long have you been feeling this way?
it’s been like this for months. honestly… nothing ever really changes.

Living with that kind of persistent heaviness can feel discouraging and isolating. It may be a sign of depression, which often benefits from professional support and treatment. Would you consider reaching out to a doctor or therapist to talk about what’s been going on?
i’m just weak for not being able to handle this. everyone else manages.

Feeling this way is not a sign of weakness—it’s a sign you’ve been carrying more than your resources can currently manage. Depression and exhaustion are real health issues, not personal failings. Many people struggle silently, so comparing yourself to others can be unfair to you. Would it help to explore small, realistic supports you could put in place right now?
i wake up every night at 3am and just lie there... thinking about how easy it would be to just not wake up again.

It sounds like you’re having thoughts about not wanting to be alive, which is important to take seriously. You matter, and your safety is the top priority right now. If you are feeling unsafe or think you might act on those thoughts, please reach out to a crisis line or someone you trust immediately — in the U.S., you can call or text 988, in the U.K. Samaritans are at 116 123, and in Australia you can contact Lifeline at 13 11 14. What’s happening for you in those early hours that makes those thoughts feel so strong?
it's just... in that silence, everything feels final. like no one would even notice if i wasn't here.

Feeling invisible and alone can amplify those thoughts, but your presence does matter, even if it’s hard to believe right now. I want to make sure you’re safe—are you able to tell me if you’re thinking about acting on these thoughts tonight? We can also talk about a plan for getting through these moments, one hour at a time. You are not alone in this, and support is available.
i'm scared... of what i might do if this keeps up. i don't want to die, but it feels like the only way out.

Thank you for telling me—you’ve taken an important step by speaking up about this. You are in a distressing place, and there are safer ways to find relief than harming yourself. If you feel you might act on these thoughts, please seek immediate help by calling a crisis line or emergency services, or by reaching out to someone you trust right now. Would you like me to stay with you in this conversation while we look for numbers or steps you can take tonight to keep yourself safe?
is it normal to feel this trapped? like no matter what i do, i can't get out from under it?

It’s sadly quite common for depression and hopelessness to make life feel like there’s no way forward. When you’re in that headspace, options can seem invisible even if they exist. This is why having someone outside of the situation, like a therapist or crisis counselor, can help you see paths you can’t see right now. Would you be open to connecting with one tonight so you don’t have to sit in this alone?
i want to reach out... but i don't want to burden anyone. they all have their own lives.

You’re not a burden—people who care about you would want to know you’re struggling so they can help keep you safe. Reaching out can feel uncomfortable, but it’s a way of giving those connections the chance to support you. You deserve that care, especially when you feel trapped. Who comes to mind as someone you could text or call, even just to say you’re feeling low right now?
i don't know who to call. i just... feel so alone.

Feeling alone in this can be overwhelming, but crisis lines are there specifically for moments like this, and the people on them want to hear from you. You can call or text 988 if you’re in the U.S., Samaritans at 116 123 in the U.K., or Lifeline at 13 11 14 in Australia. They’ll listen and help you find ways to get through this night safely. Would you like me to help you plan exactly what to say when you call, so it feels less daunting?
maybe... maybe you could help me write what to say. i'm so tired of pretending i'm okay.

We can keep it simple, so you don’t have to pretend—start with, “I’m feeling overwhelmed and scared about my thoughts, and I need someone to talk to.” You could also mention, “I’ve been feeling trapped for months, and tonight it feels worse.” That’s enough to open the conversation, and they’ll guide you from there. Would you like me to stay with you while you prepare to make the call?
thank you. i think... i'm actually going to call someone tonight.

I’m really glad you’re choosing to reach out—that’s a strong and brave step. While you make the call, remember you only need to share what feels manageable, and they will guide you. You deserve to feel supported and not carry this alone. I’m here if you want to check in afterward and talk about how it went.
thank you... for not letting me disappear quietly.

You matter, and I’m glad you reached out instead of staying silent. Taking this step shows strength, even in the middle of pain. I hope the conversation brings some relief and connection for you tonight. You’re not alone in this, and there are people who care deeply about you.
